newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel barges steady, low demand barring rise.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel barges steady, low demand barring rise.

text.p: European high sulphur barges were virtually unchanged on Thursday, with low demand blocking any market rise, traders said.
Following early offers at $86, or $1 over Wednesday's close, high sulphur barges changed hands early at $84, $84.50 and $85 fob ARA, or within the higher trading range seen since Monday.
Later, the best selling offer was at $84.50 and the best buyers were at $84 a tonne.
"It is very quiet on barges and bunker demand is also quiet," one trader said.
He said there was a large enquiry for 4,000 tonnes but doubted that would be executed today, adding otherwise total demand by mid-day was around 7,000 tonnes.
"Demand has been low throughout the week, that is why it is in this range," a second trader said. She said there was little demand for bunkers from Germany.
Low sulphur barge sellers were holding their ground at $97 a tonne for regular material, or the level the last trade was done at two days ago, while buyers moved some $1 up to the $96 mark.
Sellers were at $99 for 100 C flash material.
No trades were heard early in the day in high sulphur cargoes.

One trader said there was a number of buyers on the market looking for cracked material in northwest Europe but added that the real market was in the Mediterranean, given the open arb. Traders said one of three Russian M-100 straight-run cargoes on offer was sold late on Wednesday. The cargoes were offered at two means +$4 but it was not known if it fetched that number.
